steps.output_raw:
<think>
Need to give concrete, step-by-step instructions for Chase app/website to report card stolen and request replacement, and mention extra fraud steps. No tools apply. </think>
<plan>
1. Give precise steps in the Chase mobile app to lock/report the card stolen and request a replacement.
2. Provide equivalent steps for the Chase website as a backup.
3. Suggest calling Chase if needed and outline follow‑up actions (review transactions, update autopays).
</plan>
<action type="say">
Here’s how to get your Chase Visa blocked and replaced right now.

On the Chase mobile app:
1. Open the Chase app and sign in.  
2. Tap your stolen credit card account.  
3. Look for:  
   - “Manage card,” “Card settings,” or  
   - “Lock & unlock card” / “Replace card” / “Report lost or stolen.”  
4. Choose “Report lost or stolen” (or similar wording).  
5. Confirm that the card is STOLEN (not just lost).  
6. Make sure the options to:  
   - Block the card immediately, and  
   - Send a replacement card  
   are both selected.  
7. Confirm your mailing address and submit.

If you use the Chase website (on a computer or browser):
1. Go to chase.com and sign in.  
2. Click on your stolen credit card account.  
3. Find the card management area (often under “More…” / “Things you can do” / “Account services”).  
4. Click “Replace a card,” “Report lost or stolen,” or similar.  
5. Select “Stolen,” confirm immediate blocking and request a replacement card.  
6. Verify your shipping address and submit.

If anything in the app/website is confusing, call Chase immediately:
- Use the number on the back of any other Chase card you have, or  
- From chase.com, scroll to the bottom and use the Customer Service/“Contact Us” number.  
When connected, say: “My credit card has been stolen. Please block it immediately and send me an expedited replacement.”

Right after you’ve reported it:
1. In the app/website, review recent transactions on that card and note any you don’t recognize.  
2. Dispute any suspicious charges with Chase (they’ll guide you through it).  
3. Make a list of any subscriptions/recurring payments on that card (streaming, phone, etc.) so you can update them once the new card arrives.

Reply once you’ve gone through the steps (or if you get stuck on a particular screen) and tell me what you see—I can guide you click‑by‑click.</action>
